title: Smoother large libraries
changes: Routine recorder updates no longer rebuild an unchanged clip library, keeping controls responsive as the collection grows.
Large archives now load in manageable batches, use bounded thumbnail memory, and avoid library scans while no interface is visible.

title: Faster recent update downloads
changes: The three newest releases now remain on the update CDN for fast downloads, while older release links continue through the permanent GitHub archive.

title: Overlay waves arrive with the notification
changes: Overlay halftone waves now begin while each notification slides in, follow the moving card, and finish after it settles.

title: A softer landing for overlays
changes: Overlay notifications now settle with a compact directional halftone wave that adapts to each notification, while stopping a recording pulls its red wave inward and fades it to gray.

title: Choose your recording encoder
changes: Clips now detects usable video encoders at startup and lets you choose one in Settings; the selection is applied directly to new recordings and replays.

title: Public browser demo removed
changes: Removed the public browser demo and its simulated recordings while keeping the private local browser controls for the installed app.

title: New games are detected again
changes: Fullscreen games that are not already monitored or ignored now correctly trigger the new-game popup.

title: Faster update installation
changes: Prepared updates now avoid an unnecessary full application copy on Windows, cutting about ten seconds from installation on tested systems.

title: Release notes match your update channel
changes: Stable update users now see only stable release notes, while nightly users see the full history with stable releases clearly marked as recaps.

title: Browser opening stays in your hands
changes: Clips no longer takes control of Helium or uses its tab finder when opening the browser interface.

title: Safer updates and smoother recording
changes: Updates are now fully verified before Clips launches them.
Interrupted updates preserve the last working version instead of leaving Clips unusable.
Clips automatically rolls back if an updated version cannot start successfully.
Installation is more reliable when Windows temporarily locks application files.
Upgrades are tested from earlier stable and nightly versions before release.
New-game detection now checks whether a window actually covers its monitor.
Browsers, editors, overlays, and ordinary maximized apps are much less likely to be mistaken for games.
Large libraries load and clean up with substantially less disk activity.
Removing a recording now consistently cleans up its favorites, metadata, and thumbnails.
Recording operations are better protected against invalid or unsafe file locations.
Capture recovers more cleanly when the recording engine fails during startup.
Playback rejects damaged or invalid video data more safely.
Bundled recording and playback components are now versioned and verified for compatibility.
Fresh installations reliably include the complete browser interface and media runtime.
Clips can recover from malformed settings without silently discarding the original file.
Saved microphone selections are restored more reliably.
Background monitoring avoids duplicated work when several refreshes happen together.

title: Release archive cleanup
changes: GitHub's full release history now keeps nightly builds in numeric order across every page while existing Clips download addresses continue to work.

title: Release history ordering
changes: Nightly release tags now remain in the correct newest-first order on GitHub once their sequence reaches two digits.

title: Recovery and release safeguards
changes: Clips now rolls back automatically when an updated application cannot complete its first healthy startup, and validates the full staged application before launching it.
Malformed settings are safely normalized or preserved for recovery instead of breaking monitoring or being silently overwritten.
Large recording libraries perform less repeated disk work, cleanup no longer rescans the full library after every deletion, and overlapping monitor runs are serialized.
Browser pairing, native player frame allocation, runtime ABI checks, native CI builds, and public release verification now fail closed in unsafe or inconsistent states.
Release tests clean up their temporary media runtimes, Worker routes have behavioral coverage, and JavaScript correctness linting is part of the standard check.

title: Staged updater diagnostic test
changes: This release exercises the instrumented staged updater from the previous nightly without changing recording behavior.

title: Forensic staged updater
changes: Staged updates now use Electron's raw filesystem for app.asar, retry preparation five times, preserve failed attempts, and record detailed sanitized diagnostics that can be copied from Settings.

title: Classic installer updates restored
changes: Updates once again use the proven NSIS installer download and restart flow instead of custom app-version folders.

title: Updater recovery validation
changes: This release validates the repaired staged-update path introduced in the previous nightly, without changing recording behavior.

title: Update preparation protected from cleanup
changes: Startup cleanup now completes before downloading updates and never removes a fresh preparation folder owned by an overlapping updater process.

title: Microphone selection restored
changes: Settings now restore the saved microphone before device discovery, preventing unrelated autosaves from silently switching microphone recording off.

title: Verified application packages during updates
changes: Clips now cryptographically verifies app.asar after extraction, after Windows copy fallback, and before reusing a prepared update.

title: Cleaner internals and reproducible checks
changes: Media serving and tray management now live in focused modules, reducing Electron lifecycle coupling without changing app behavior.
The standard check now validates Worker configuration, generated types, and browser assets entirely in a temporary directory using checked-in example configuration.

title: Updates that survive persistent Windows locks
changes: Update preparation now falls back to a verified directory copy when Windows keeps the extracted update folder locked too long to rename.

title: Safer, smoother recording libraries
changes: Recording file operations now reject junctions that escape the library, and deleted recordings immediately lose playback access.
Large libraries are scanned without blocking the app, while automatic cleanup also removes favorites, metadata, and cached thumbnails.
Capture settings, native player transport, and capture-engine process handling are more resilient to malformed input and rare Windows races.
Clean Windows CI now exercises application checks and both native hosts.

title: Media runtime recovery after interrupted updates
changes: Clips can now reconcile a stale runtime manifest when an interrupted slim update already installed a verified bundled native component, while continuing to reject unverified runtime corruption.

title: Updates that finish safely on Windows
changes: Update preparation no longer races its own stale-file cleanup, and final installation retries short-lived Windows file locks.
Release testing now protects the active build, rollback build, and in-progress update together while exercising locked-directory recovery.

title: Reliable media startup after updates
changes: Update cleanup now preserves the active and currently running application package, preventing media runtime files from disappearing during startup.

title: Updates that fail safely
changes: Update requests now time out cleanly, and interrupted preparations can no longer displace a working rollback version.
Release feeds and artifacts are verified cryptographically, and feed publication rolls back if either metadata format fails.
Release builds test upgrades from representative stable and nightly clients, runtime migration, restart behavior, and package inventory before publication.
Installer and staged update packages now carry a consistent player runtime.

title: Safer installs and capture recovery
changes: Fresh installers now include the complete browser interface.
Media runtime updates install transactionally with integrity checks and preserve the previous working runtime if installation fails.
The capture engine now cleans up safely after initialization failures and can recover without retaining partial OBS state.
Recording library and storage behavior now lives in a focused, behavior-tested service instead of the main application lifecycle module.

title: Game detection that understands fullscreen
changes: New-game prompts now require a window to cover its monitor, preventing ordinary maximized apps, editors, browsers, and overlays from being mistaken for games.

title: Faster release delivery
changes: Release builds and uploads now run independent work concurrently, substantially reducing the time required to ship fixes and new features.

title: New game detection and permanent releases
changes: Clips detects sustained game-sized windows outside the monitored list and shows in-game shortcuts to add or ignore them.
Capture automatically recovers from an unresponsive engine after GPU encoder failures.
Installers, update packages, and corresponding source are permanently archived together on GitHub Releases while existing update addresses continue to work.

title: Complete release archive migration
changes: Stable installers and update packages now share the same permanent GitHub archive and backward-compatible download redirects as nightly releases.
GitHub release titles use the same concise 0.4-commit format shown inside Clips instead of exposing the updater's internal SemVer.

title: Reliable release archiving
changes: Historical corresponding-source archives can now be safely verified on GitHub before their redundant R2 copies are removed.

title: Permanent release downloads
changes: Release installers, update packages, and corresponding source are now archived together on GitHub Releases while existing Clips update addresses continue to work.

title: New game detection
changes: Clips now notices sustained, game-sized windows that are not in the monitored list and shows in-game shortcuts to add or permanently ignore them.

title: Capture recovers after encoder failures
changes: Clips now replaces an unresponsive capture engine after a GPU encoder failure, allowing recording to restart instead of repeatedly timing out.

title: Browser focus works in Helium
changes: Opening Clips now finds its existing tab in Helium and other Chromium browsers even when the browser hides its tab strip from Windows accessibility tools.

title: Opening Clips finds its browser tab
changes: Double-clicking Clips or choosing Open now selects the existing Clips browser tab and brings its browser window forward instead of appearing to do nothing.
Idle instant replay now has its own length setting, defaulting to five minutes, while using the same Save clip button and shortcut as normal recording clips.

title: Never miss the last five minutes
changes: Added an opt-in Instant replay while idle setting that keeps only the latest clip-length window when full recording is off, letting Save clip recover moments without filling the drive with a full session.

title: Browser tabs survive restarts
changes: The browser interface now reconnects after Clips or an update restarts, and tray actions wait briefly for the surviving tab before opening a new one.

title: Quieter warnings and one browser tab
changes: Frame-drop overlays now appear only for meaningful bursts or sustained loss, while small isolated misses remain available in diagnostics.
Opening Clips reuses its connected browser interface instead of continuously creating duplicate tabs.

title: AMD fix for existing installations
changes: AMD hardware encoder support now installs directly into existing capture runtimes as well as fresh installations.

title: AMD encoding and safer diagnostics
changes: Restored AMD AMF hardware encoder detection by adding the helper OBS requires to both existing and fresh capture runtimes.
Local diagnostic logs now redact Windows usernames, capture-device identifiers, and window titles.
Stopped high-frequency microphone meter polling from flooding diagnostic logs.

title: Complete overlay warning cards
changes: Fixed multi-line capture warnings and error notifications being cut off along their bottom edge.

title: Clearer loading and reliable fullscreen
changes: Browser playback now shows a centered spinner while a recording starts, seeks, or buffers.
Entering browser fullscreen keeps the current clip alive, provides fullscreen playback controls, and restores the same player session when fullscreen closes.

title: Withdrawn updates cannot restart
changes: Restart to update now re-downloads and authenticates the current update metadata before stopping capture or relaunching, preventing a prepared build from installing after it has been withdrawn or replaced.
When an update was replaced, Clips downloads the current replacement; when it was pulled entirely, Clips reports that it was withdrawn and leaves the app running.

title: Startup disk activity fixed
changes: Clips no longer repeatedly initializes and shuts down the capture engine to refresh microphone settings after every live browser update, eliminating the severe disk activity and startup instability introduced in the previous nightly.
Automatic deletion of incomplete browser preview caches has been removed from startup; cache cleanup will not block or overload the app.

title: Playback closes quietly
changes: Closing a browser video or seeking no longer shows intermittent JavaScript EPIPE error dialogs when the previous media stream disconnects normally.

title: Fast, responsive browser playback
changes: Opening a recording in the browser now starts a paced stream instead of copying the entire file first, keeping recording controls, update checks, disk usage, and the rest of the computer responsive even with very large sessions.
Browser playback can seek without building multi-gigabyte preview files, while media preparation and thumbnail work no longer monopolize the app.

title: Browser controls stay connected
changes: The local browser interface now stays connected to Clips, so recording controls, settings, thumbnails, and playback continue using the installed app instead of falling back to demo data.
Library thumbnails load when the Library is opened, settings refresh across open interfaces, and the browser-demo banner no longer appears on the private local interface.

title: Browser UI connection fixed
changes: The experimental browser interface now opens from Clips on a private localhost page, avoiding browser security rules that blocked clips.jss.fi from reaching the installed app.
Connect Clips on the web demo now hands off to the working local browser interface, where recordings and controls stay on this computer.

title: Use Clips from the web
changes: An experimental Desktop window switch can now hand the interface over to clips.jss.fi/app while the installed app keeps recording, handling shortcuts, and showing overlays in the background.

The browser interface can securely pair with the local Clips gateway, control recording and settings, receive live updates, and play or edit recordings without uploading them. When Clips is unavailable, the same page remains an interactive demo.

title: Faster update downloads
changes: Updates now use several verified download streams at once, allowing fast internet connections to finish downloading much sooner while retaining compatibility with older servers.

title: Library sorting that matches its labels
changes: Largest first now ranks the entire Library in one list instead of sorting separately inside each day, while Game groups the whole Library by game; only chronological sorts retain day sections.

title: Consistent shortcut controls
changes: The marker shortcut now uses the same click-and-press capture control as the clip shortcut, and both shortcuts have a dedicated Disable button.

title: Clear update-ready state
changes: The Check now button stays disabled after an update finishes downloading and changes to Update ready, preventing redundant update checks while the restart action is available.

title: Cleaner markers and library controls
changes: Timeline markers are now a shortcut-only feature with a clear setting to disable them, while keeping the in-game saved confirmation.
Search and sorting now appear in the Library instead of today's Recent view, with readable native dropdown colors.
New replays, trims, compilations, and desktop captures retain their game identity; older footage is clearly labeled when its game cannot be recovered.

title: From recording to finished highlight
changes: Added timeline markers with a dedicated shortcut so memorable moments can be flagged without creating extra replay files.
The library can now search and sort clips, with editable titles and tags stored without modifying video files.
Monitored games can override capture quality, resolution, frame rate, and replay length with per-game profiles.
Storage settings now show total library usage, free drive space, and a per-game breakdown.
Selected clips can be stitched into a single compilation while preserving their chosen order.
Capture settings now include a five-second local microphone recording and playback test.

title: Capture health warnings
changes: Added in-game overlay warnings when recording frames drop, with a quick explanation of whether the GPU or video encoder could not keep up.
Capture and application errors now appear in the overlay with their reason instead of being visible only in the Clips window.

title: Clear remove buttons
changes: Fixed the remove icon in monitored game and audio application lists so it displays as a clear remove symbol instead of garbled text.

title: Easier application audio selection
changes: Audio routing now lets you choose running applications from a list and remove them individually, matching the monitored-game picker.

title: Complete open-source release materials
changes: Installers now include the complete Clips, 7-Zip, OBS, and MPV license notices, and every release publishes a permanent corresponding-source bundle.

title: Clips in the browser
changes: Added an interactive browser demo at clips.jss.fi/app so the interface can be explored without installing the Windows app.

title: Authenticated application updates
changes: Application updates now require a valid Ed25519 release signature before Clips downloads or runs them.
Release uploads now use separate bucket-scoped R2 credentials instead of a broad Wrangler login.

title: Native capture fixes that actually stick
changes: Prevented older Clips executables from overwriting the shared HDR and microphone engine after losing the single-instance lock.
Update restarts now shut down the capture engine before replacing native components, with retries for briefly locked files.
Added explicit diagnostics confirming whether NVIDIA microphone noise removal is attached and enabled.

title: Privacy-first About page
changes: Redesigned About settings to put privacy and data controls first, with a clear statement that recordings remain on your computer.
Reorganized app details, updates, diagnostics, and release history into clearer sections.

title: Adaptive HDR tone mapping
changes: HDR-to-SDR recordings now use the active display's Windows-reported SDR-white and peak-brightness levels instead of fixed values that could severely blow out highlights.
Capture logs now report the selected display and tone-mapping reference level for easier HDR troubleshooting.

title: Reliable update restarts
changes: Clips now opens its main window after a user-triggered update restart, even when it originally launched in the background.
Added an export-quality dropdown directly to the Trim editor and kept it synchronized with Editor settings.

title: Focused editor settings
changes: Removed the unfinished custom CDN upload integration and its credential settings.
Renamed Integrations settings to Editor so the remaining trim-quality option is easier to find.

title: Complete desktop recordings
changes: Manual desktop recordings now include all system playback audio, so browsers and other non-allow-listed apps can be heard.
The embedded player now keeps a consistent height when switching into the editor.

title: Persistent window controls
changes: The recording controls and Windows title-bar buttons now remain in a reserved top row across the library, Settings, and clip player.
The clip player stays below the title bar at compact window sizes instead of covering content behind the native window buttons.

title: Reliable overlay and commit nightlies
changes: Improved overlay topmost behavior and automatic recovery after renderer or loading failures.
Made game-window detection resilient to windows disappearing during a process scan.
Added overlay diagnostics for readiness, monitor placement, bounds, and topmost state.
Nightly builds now carry the short commit hash that identifies their source snapshot.

title: Live audio mixing
changes: Simplified the recording player to a single Edit action with the close button kept at the top right.
Audio source sliders and mute controls now update playback immediately without modifying the clip until Save is pressed.

title: Dedicated clip editor
changes: Replaced the player Edit menu with direct Trim and Audio actions.
Added a dedicated editor workspace with a large video preview and persistent Mix and Trim sidebar tabs.

title: Editing inside the player
changes: Moved Trim and Volume mix out of clip-card menus and into the recording player.
Playback now stays visible while adjusting individual audio source tracks.

title: True multi-track audio
changes: New recordings and replays now keep application and microphone audio on named, independently editable tracks.
Volume mixing rebuilds the default playback mix while preserving the source tracks and original video quality.

title: Clip volume mixer
changes: Added per-track volume and mute controls with options to update a clip or save a new mixed copy.
Moved clip editing actions into a compact three-dot menu.

title: Stable update checks
changes: Manual update checks are now available on both stable and nightly channels.

title: Startup reliability and changelog
changes: Stopped transient process-list output from surfacing as a startup error.
Added this scrolling release history to the About page.
Consolidated updates and telemetry behind clips.jss.fi.

title: First stable release
changes: Introduced separate stable and nightly update channels.
Raw recording thumbnails now skip the black frames before game capture appears.
Added optional anonymous version or diagnostic telemetry.
Bundled complete third-party licensing notices and source information.

title: Development releases
changes: Built the native libobs recording and replay-buffer engine.
Added per-application audio, MPV playback, trimming, storage cleanup, and restart-only updates.
Redesigned the recording library, settings, tray controls, and in-game notifications.
